facts.statement: Rhomaleosaurus is an extinct genus of rhomaleosaurid pliosauroid known from Northamptonshire and Yorkshire in the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Rhomaleosaurus (meaning "strong lizard") is an extinct genus of Early Jurassic (Toarcian age, about 183 to 175.6 million years ago) rhomaleosaurid pliosauroid known from Northamptonshire and from Yorkshire of the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The genus was first named by Harry Seeley in 1874, with Rhomaleosaurus cramptoni designated as the type species.
facts.quote: It was first named by Harry Seeley in 1874 and the type species is Rhomaleosaurus cramptoni.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was unearthed in July 1848 at an alum quarry near Whitby, Yorkshire, England.
facts.quote: In July 1848, a fossil of a large plesiosaur was unearthed in an alum quarry at Kettleness, near Whitby, in Yorkshire, England.

facts.statement: The fossil dates to the early Toarcian age, approximately 183 to 180 million years ago, based on the A. bifrons ammonite zone.
facts.quote: It was collected from the A. bifrons ammonite zone of the Whitby Mudstone Formation, dating to the early Toarcian age, about 183 to 180 million years ago.

facts.statement: The complete skeleton, NMING F8785, was kept at Mulgrave Castle for five years before being moved to Dublin.
facts.quote: The complete skeleton which preserved the skull, NMING F8785, was kept for five years at Mulgrave Castle, which was then owned by the Marquess of Normanby.

facts.statement: The fossil was introduced to Sir Philip Crampton in 1853 by the Marquess of Normanby.
facts.quote: In 1853, the Marquess introduced the interesting finding to the eminent Irish surgeon and anatomist, Sir Philip Crampton.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley erected the new genus Rhomaleosaurus in 1874 based on this finding.
facts.quote: In 1874, the British geologist Harry Govier Seeley, based on this finding, which is now known as the type genus of the family Rhomaleosauridae, recognized and erected a new genus establishing Rhomaleosaurus.

facts.statement: The skull of the holotype specimen was finally prepared in 2006, enabling a restudy of the genus.
facts.quote: Only in 2006 the skull of this specimen was finally prepared which enabled a restudy of this genus.

facts.statement: R. propinquus is known from the holotype WM 852.S, an articulated almost complete skeleton preserving the skull.
facts.quote: R. propinquus is known from the holotype WM 852.S, articulated almost complete skeleton which preserved the skull, exposed in dorsal view.

facts.statement: R. propinquus lived during the middle Toarcian stage, approximately 180 to 177 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was collected from the A. serpentines ammonoid zone, of the Whitby Mudstone Formation, Yorkshire, England, dating to the middle Toarcian stage, about 180-177 million years ago.

facts.statement: R. propinquus was first named by Tate and Blake in 1876 as a new species of Plesiosaurus.
facts.quote: R. propinquus was first named by Tate and Blake in 1876 as a new species of Plesiosaurus.

facts.statement: R. thorntoni is known from the holotype NHMUK PV R 4853, a partially complete skeleton preserving most of the skull and mandibles.
facts.quote: R. thorntoni is known from the holotype NHMUK PV R 4853, three-dimensional, partially complete skeleton which preserved most of the skull and mandibles.

facts.statement: R. thorntoni was collected by Henry Gerard Thornton from Kingsthorp, Northamptonshire.
facts.quote: It was collected by Henry Gerard Thornton from Kingsthorp of Northamptonshire, dating to the Toarcian stage.

facts.statement: R. thorntoni was first named by Andrews in 1922 and later revised as a junior synonym of R. cramptoni.
facts.quote: R. thorntoni was first named by Andrews in 1922 and later revised by Cruickshank (1996) as a junior synonym of R. cramptoni, alongside R. zetlandicus.

facts.statement: R. zetlandicus is known from the holotype YORYM G503, a nearly complete skull and vertebral column associated with parts of the limbs.
facts.quote: R. zetlandicus is known from the holotype YORYM G503 (pictured), a nearly complete skull and vertebral column in association with parts of the limbs.

facts.statement: The specimen was collected in the early 1850s from the Alum Shale of Whitby Mudstone Formation and donated to the Yorkshire Philosophical Society in 1852.
facts.quote: It was in the early 1850s collected from the Alum Shale of Whitby Mudstone Formation, Yorkshire, dating from the Toarcian stage and donated in 1852 to the Yorkshire Philosophical Society by Lawrence Dundas, 1st Earl of Zetland, the Loftus mine owner.

facts.statement: R. zetlandicus was first validly named by Phillips in 1854, and its skull was described in detail by Michael Alan Taylor in 1992.
facts.quote: R. zetlandicus was first validly named by Phillips in 1854 and its skull was described in detail by Michael Alan Taylor in 1992.

facts.statement: Cruickshank (1996) revised R. zetlandicus as a senior synonym of R. cramptoni, with R. thorntoni as a junior synonym.
facts.quote: Later the taxon was revised by Cruickshank (1996) as a senior synonym of R. cramptoni, R. thorntoni being a junior synonym.

facts.statement: Smith and Dyke (2008) recognized R. propinquus as a valid species.
facts.quote: Smith and Dyke (2008) also recognized R. propinquus as valid.

facts.statement: Smith (2007) and Smith and Dyke (2008) argued that R. megacephalus belongs to Eurycleidus and R. victor represents the new genus Meyerasaurus.
facts.quote: Smith (2007) and Smith and Dyke (2008) pointed out that these species do not belong to Rhomaleosaurus, as R. megacephalus is referred to Eurycleidus (or to a new genus by Smith and Dyke (2008)) and R. victor represents a new genus named Meyerasaurus by Smith and Vincent in 2010.

facts.statement: Specimens previously regarded as Thaumatosaurus now represent the holotypes of Eurycleidus, Meyerasaurus, and Rhomaleosaurus.
facts.quote: The diagnostic specimens which previously were regarded as Thaumatosauruss specimens, now represent the holotypes of Eurycleidus, Meyerasaurus and Rhomaleosaurus.

facts.statement: This adaptation would have enabled Rhomaleosaurus to hunt its prey in a manner similar to some modern shark species.
facts.quote: This adaptation would have enabled it to hunt its prey in a similar manner to some modern shark species.

facts.statement: Rhomaleosaurus coexisted with the ichthyosaur Temnodontosaurus, and both acted as top-tier consumers feeding on ammonites, plesiosaurs, and ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Rhomaleosaurus coexisted with the extinct ichthyosaur Temnodontosaurus in which both acted as top-tier consumers with both feeding on ammonites, plesiosaurs, and ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil of Rhomaleosaurus was unearthed in July 1848 at the Alum quarry near Whitby, Yorkshire, England.
facts.quote: En julio de 1848, el fósil de un plesiosaurio grande fue desenterrado en la cantera Alum en Kettleness, cerca de Whitby, en Yorkshire, Inglaterra.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen dates to the early Toarcian stage, between 183 and 180 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fue recolectado de la zona del ammonite A. bifrons de la Formación Whitby Mudstone, que data de principios del Toarciano, entre 183 a 180 millones de años.

facts.statement: In 1853, the Marquis presented the fossil to the Irish surgeon and anatomist Sir Philip Crampton.
facts.quote: En 1853, el marqués presentó el interesante hallazgo al eminente cirujano y anatomista irlandés, Sir Philip Crampton.

facts.statement: In 1874, British geologist Harry G. Seeley recognized the specimen as a distinct genus and established the name Rhomaleosaurus.
facts.quote: En 1874, el geólogo británico Harry G. Seeley, basándose en este hallazgo, el cual es ahora conocido como el holotipo de la familia Rhomaleosauridae, lo reconoció como un género distinto y estableció la nueva denominación de Rhomaleosaurus.

facts.statement: The skull of the holotype was not finally prepared and described until 2006, allowing for a re-study of the genus.
facts.quote: Sólo hasta 2006 el cráneo de este espécimen fue descrito fue finalmente preparado y permitió así un reestudio del género.

facts.statement: The species R. thorntoni was recovered from Kingsthorp in Northamptonshire, dating to the Toarcian stage.
facts.quote: Fue recuperado de Kingsthorp en Northamptonshire, datando de la etapa del Toarciano.

facts.statement: The species R. zetlandicus was collected from the Alum Shale of the Whitby Mudstone Formation in Yorkshire, dating to the Toarcian stage.
facts.quote: Fue recolectado del Esquisto Alum de la Formación Whitby Mudstone, en Yorkshire, datando de la etapa del Toarciano.

facts.statement: According to Smith (2007), the genus Rhomaleosaurus comprises only three valid species: R. cramptoni, R. thorntoni, and R. zetlandicus.
facts.quote: de acuerdo a Smith (2007), en su tesis sobre la anatomía y clasificación de la familia Rhomaleosauridae, el género Rhomaleosaurus sólo abarca tres especies válidas: R. cramptoni, R. thorntoni y R. zetlandicus.

facts.statement: Smith (2007) and Smith & Dyke (2008) determined that R. megacephalus belongs to Eurycleidus (or a new genus) and R. victor represents a new genus named Meyerasaurus.
facts.quote: Smith (2007) y Smith y Dyke (2008) señalaron que estas especies no pertenecían a Rhomaleosaurus, y R. megacephalus es referido a Eurycleidus (o a un nuevo género según Smith y Dyke (2008)) mientras que R. victor representa un nuevo género llamado Meyerasaurus por Smith y Vincent en 2010.

facts.statement: Today, the taxon Thaumatosaurus is considered a nomen dubium because its holotype can at most be classified as an indeterminate Pliosauroidea.
facts.quote: Hoy en día este taxón es considerado como un nomen dubium debido a que su holotipo puede como mucho ser clasificado como un Pliosauroidea indeterminado.

facts.statement: Specimens previously considered as Thaumatosaurus now represent the holotypes of Eurycleidus, Meyerasaurus, and Rhomaleosaurus.
facts.quote: Los especímenes que fueron previamente considerados como ejemplares de Thaumatosaurus, ahora representan los holotipos de Eurycleidus, Meyerasaurus y Rhomaleosaurus.

facts.statement: Rhomaleosaurus may have been capable of detecting scents while submerged by forcing water through passages in its skull containing sensory organs.
facts.quote: Rhomaleosaurus puede haber sido capaz de captar olores mientras estaba sumergido, forzando el agua a través de pasajes en su cráneo que contenían los órganos sensoriales.

facts.statement: The parent group of Rhomaleosaurus is Rhomaleosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Rhomaleosauridae

facts.statement: The time range for Rhomaleosaurus is from the Hettangian to the Toarcian, between 201.4 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Toarcian (201.4 to 174.7 million years ago)
